prd_non_functional_refs: non_functional.performance — Dashboard sub-second; data-entry form save < 500 ms; Sales Report < 2s for 1 year unfiltered
non_functional.security — All inputs validated server-side (V2 layers JWT auth + RBAC + bcrypt hashing on top of V1 posture)
hld_risks_covered: R-001 severity=critical (stock ledger race) — regression via IS-018 concurrent invoice+payment path is out of V2 system scope; V2 tests focus on V2-introduced surface
R-004 severity=medium (V1 no-auth) — MITIGATED by V2 T-092 auth guard; ST-015..ST-020 verify the mitigation
RI-V2-001 informational (SECRET_KEY handling) — ST-016 (signature tamper) implicitly verifies signature verification is enforced
RI-V2-002 informational (zero-price fallback) — out of system-test scope; already covered by TC-181 unit path
notes: One scenario per critical NFR + one per relevant risk mitigation. Numeric thresholds are recorded as the target; the executed test records the actual median/p95 alongside.

Performance thresholds use median over 20 calls (matches S3 test_perf_dashboard.py style) rather than pytest-benchmark to avoid a new plugin dependency. Median is the load-representative statistic for a single-user internal deployment (PRD non_functional.scalability: single-digit concurrent).

Security scenarios exercise the JWT contract at the edge — expired token, tampered signature, alg=none header, SQL-injection in username, deactivated user, and role gating — all against real HTTP via TestClient.
Boundary scenarios use @pytest.mark.parametrize with mixed pass/fail inputs to bound the accepted-value surface (AC-066 export formats; AC-072/AC-073 payment overpayment).
Error-handling scenarios use direct calls with the conflicting payload asserting the exact HTTP code (AC-067 duplicate price, AC-070 duplicate invoice).

scenarios.description: POST /auth/login round-trip latency (bcrypt verify + JWT sign + DB read). Verifies the auth path stays within the PRD 'form save < 500 ms' budget on the reference workstation.
scenarios.how: Seed one active SUPERVISOR user with a bcrypt-hashed password. Time 20 sequential POST /api/v1/auth/login calls with correct credentials via TestClient. Assert status 200 on every call and statistics.median(durations_ms) < 500.

scenarios.nfr_ref: non_functional.performance (Sales Report < 2s analog for Inward Report)
scenarios.description: GET /reports/inward with no filters over ~120 inward transaction rows. Verifies the V2 inward-report read path stays within the 2s Sales-Report analog even with a year's worth of small-shop data.
scenarios.how: Seed 3 designs × 2 grades = 6 pairs and 120 inward transactions distributed across dates. Time 10 sequential GET /api/v1/reports/inward via TestClient. Assert 200 + reconciliation invariant (sum txn nos == sum consolidation nos) on the first call, then median duration < 2000ms.

scenarios.nfr_ref: non_functional.security (V2 auth guard mitigation of R-004)
scenarios.description: Expired JWT (exp in the past) must be rejected by get_current_user with HTTP 401 on both a V1 and a V2 protected endpoint. Verifies python-jose exp claim enforcement.
scenarios.threshold: GET /suppliers and GET /invoices with an expired-token Bearer header both return 401
scenarios.how: Mint a token via create_access_token(..., expires_delta=timedelta(seconds=-1)). GET /api/v1/suppliers and GET /api/v1/invoices with that token. Assert both == 401.

scenarios.description: JWT whose signature was signed with a different SECRET_KEY must be rejected with HTTP 401. Verifies HS256 signature is actually verified server-side (guards against dev-key leak → prod-token forgery).
scenarios.threshold: GET /suppliers with a foreign-signed Bearer token returns 401
scenarios.how: jwt.encode({sub: user, role: SUPERVISOR, exp: future}, 'ATTACKER-KEY', algorithm='HS256'). GET /api/v1/suppliers with that Bearer. Assert 401.

scenarios.description: JWT with alg=none header (unsigned) must be rejected with HTTP 401. Verifies the decoder does not accept 'none' as a valid signature algorithm despite server default being HS256.
scenarios.threshold: GET /suppliers with an alg=none token returns 401
scenarios.how: Build a token manually: base64url({alg:'none', typ:'JWT'}) + '.' + base64url({sub:'X',role:'SUPERVISOR',exp:future}) + '.' (empty signature). GET /api/v1/suppliers. Assert 401.

scenarios.description: SQL injection payloads in POST /auth/login username field must return HTTP 401 (auth fail) and MUST NOT produce HTTP 500 (SQL error leak) or bypass authentication.
scenarios.how: @pytest.mark.parametrize over 4 canonical payloads: "' OR '1'='1", "admin' --", "'; DROP TABLE tbl_user_master;--", "' UNION SELECT NULL,NULL,NULL--". POST /api/v1/auth/login with each as username, random password. Assert every response.status_code == 401. Assert tbl_user_master row-count unchanged post-run.

scenarios.description: A user deactivated (is_active=False) mid-token-life must be rejected on the next authenticated request with HTTP 401 even though the JWT itself is still valid (not expired, correct signature). Verifies is_active is checked on every request, not cached in the token.
scenarios.threshold: GET /suppliers with a still-valid Bearer for a deactivated user returns 401
scenarios.how: Seed active user U + mint valid token T. Flip U.is_active=False and commit. GET /api/v1/suppliers with Bearer T. Assert 401.

scenarios.description: STAFF-role token must be rejected with HTTP 403 on SUPERVISOR-only endpoints. Verifies require_supervisor DI factory enforces the role gate (not just get_current_user).
scenarios.threshold: POST /users, POST /prices, POST /invoices with STAFF Bearer all return 403
scenarios.how: Seed one active STAFF user + mint STAFF token. Issue POST /api/v1/users (minimal valid body), POST /api/v1/prices (minimal valid body), POST /api/v1/invoices?sales_header_id=999 with that Bearer. Assert every response is 403.

scenarios.description: GET /reports/{sales,inward}/export accepts only format=pdf|xlsx and rejects every other format with HTTP 400.
scenarios.how: @pytest.mark.parametrize over accepted (pdf, xlsx) and rejected (csv, xml, txt, json, HTML, empty) values. GET /api/v1/reports/sales/export?format=X and /reports/inward/export?format=X. Assert accepted returns 200 with correct Content-Type; rejected returns 400.

scenarios.nfr_ref: AC-072 / AC-073 (F-019) — payment status computation + overpayment guard
scenarios.description: Payment amounts near the invoice total must produce the correct status; any amount that would push cumulative payments strictly above total_amount must return HTTP 422.
scenarios.threshold: amount < total → PARTIAL, amount == total → PAID, amount > total → 422, second payment where cumulative > total → 422
scenarios.how: Seed a fresh sales+invoice with total_amount=1000.00. @pytest.mark.parametrize over (amount, expected_status, expected_state): (500.00, 201, 'PARTIAL'), (1000.00, 201, 'PAID'), (1000.01, 422, None), then a sequence test: pay 600 (PARTIAL) then attempt 401 (422 — cumulative 1001 > 1000).

scenarios.description: POST /prices with a (design_id, grade_id, effective_from) triple that already exists returns HTTP 409.
scenarios.threshold: second POST /prices with identical triple returns 409
scenarios.how: Seed masters (design=1, grade=1). POST /api/v1/prices {design_id:1, grade_id:1, effective_from:2026-01-01, unit_price:'100.00'} — expect 201. POST same body — assert 409. Body of second response must not contain a Python stack trace.

scenarios.description: POST /invoices?sales_header_id=N a second time for the same sales_header_id returns HTTP 409 (uq_invoice_header_sales_header_id).
scenarios.threshold: second POST /invoices for the same sale returns 409
scenarios.how: Seed 1 design + 1 grade + 1 dealer + 1 staff + 1 price. POST /api/v1/sales for that pair. POST /api/v1/invoices?sales_header_id={id} — expect 201. POST same URL — assert 409.
